Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 30, verse 1:

Naming of the Surah

• It is called al-Rum (the Romans), because it opens with the report about the Romans and the victory that will be theirs in the future. This word does not occur in the Noble Qur'an except at the opening of this surah.

From the Aims of the Surah

• Demonstrating the inimitability (i'jaz) of the Qur'an by reporting future matters whose occurrence was confirmed, such as the Romans' defeat of the Persians after the Persians had defeated the Romans, and reassuring the believers and calming their souls with this.

• Discussing the sights of the universe and of life, and the wonders of God's power in His many signs in this world, as a proof of the existence of the Mighty Creator and a drawing of attention to the signs of the One, the Subduer.

• Discussing the possibility of resurrection after death through rational and sensory evidence, among which: that restoring creation is, by the logic of reason, easier than originating it, and that the revival of the earth after its death by rain is evidence of revival after annihilation.

• Praising this religion and the virtues to which it calls, urging the Prophet (ﷺ) and the Muslims to hold fast to it, giving rights to those who deserve them, and alerting to the condition of the polytheists and their vices.

• Coining parables to show the falsehood of polytheism, describing the polytheists as ignorant and as neglecting reflection on the Hereafter, and not taking heed from the destruction of earlier nations similar to them in associating partners with God, and explaining their condition at their resurrection and their excuses for what they previously did.

[Tafsir]

﴿Alif. Lam. Mim.﴾ The discussion of the disjointed letters (al-huruf al-muqatta'ah) has already been covered at the beginning of Surat al-Baqarah.

The Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on Surah 30, verses 2–5:

The Persians overcame the Romans in the nearest land (to the Romans), "al-Sham" (the Levant), to "Fars" (Persia). But after their defeat, the Romans will overcome the Persians within a period of time, not exceeding ten years nor less than three. To Allah, the Exalted, belongs the command entirely, before the Romans' victory and after it. On the day the Romans triumph over the Persians, the believers will rejoice in Allah's victory for the Romans over the Persians. Allah, the Exalted, grants victory to whom He wills and abandons whom He wills, and He is the Mighty who cannot be overcome, the Merciful toward whomever He wills of His creation. This was fulfilled: the Romans overcame the Persians after seven years, and the Muslims rejoiced at that, because the Romans were People of the Book, even though they had distorted it.

God has promised the believers a firm promise that will not be broken: the victory of the Byzantine Romans, who were Christians, over the Persians, who were idolaters. But most of the disbelievers of Mecca do not know that what God has promised is true. They only know the outward appearances of the worldly life and its adornments, and they are heedless of the matters of the Hereafter and of what would benefit them therein; they do not reflect upon them.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 30, verse 8:

Have these deniers, who deny the messengers of God and the meeting with Him, not reflected upon God's creation of them, and that He created them when they were nothing? God did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them except with truth, for establishing justice, reward and punishment, and as evidence of His oneness and power, and for a specified term at whose end they will arrive, which is the Day of Resurrection. Yet indeed many of the people are disbelievers in the meeting with their Lord, denying it out of ignorance that their return is to God after their annihilation, and out of heedlessness of the Hereafter.

Have these deniers of God, who are heedless of the Hereafter, not travelled through the land, observing and reflecting, so that they might see what became of the nations before them who denied the messengers of God, such as ʿAd and Thamud? They were stronger than these people in body, and more capable of enjoying life: they ploughed the land and cultivated it, and they built palaces and dwelt in them. They built up their world more than the people of Makkah have built up theirs, yet their building and their long lifespans did not benefit them. Their messengers came to them with clear proofs and manifest evidences, but they denied them, so God destroyed them. God did not wrong them by that destruction; rather, they wronged themselves through polytheism and disobedience.

Then the end of those who did evil, from among the tyrants and disbelievers, was the worst and most grievous of ends, because they denied God and mocked His signs that He sent down upon His messengers.

Allah alone is the One who uniquely originates all creatures, and He alone is able to bring them back again a second time. Then to Him all creation will return, and He will reward the good-doer for his good and the evildoer for his evil.

Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 30, verse 12:

On the day the Hour (al-Sa'ah) is established, the criminals (al-mujrimun) will despair of escaping the punishment, and bewilderment will overtake them, so their argument will be cut off.

It was said regarding the verse, "Then the polytheists will have no intercessors from among their gods that they used to worship besides Allah on that Day. Rather, those gods will disown them, and they will disown those gods. So intercession belongs to Allah alone, and it must not be sought from anyone else."

On the day the Hour is established, the people of faith and the people of disbelief will be separated. As for those who believed in Allah and His Messenger and did righteous deeds, they will be in Paradise, honored, gladdened, and blessed with bounties.

On the day the Hour is established, the people of faith and the people of disbelief will be separated. As for those who believed in Allah and His Messenger and did righteous deeds, they will be in Paradise, honored, gladdened, and blessed with bounties.

And as for those who disbelieved in Allah, denied what the messengers brought, and rejected the resurrection after death, they will remain in the punishment, as a recompense for what they denied in the world.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 30, verses 17–18:

O believers, glorify God and declare Him free of any partner, consort, or offspring. Describe Him with the attributes of perfection with your tongues, and realize that through all your limbs, when you enter the evening, when you enter the morning, in the late afternoon, and at midday. To Him, glorified is He, belong praise and commendation in the heavens and the earth, and in the night and the day.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 30, verses 17–18:

O believers, glorify God and declare Him free of any partner, consort, or offspring. Describe Him with the attributes of perfection with your tongues, and realize that through all your limbs, when you enter the evening, when you enter the morning, in the late afternoon, and at midday. To Him, glorified is He, belong praise and commendation in the heavens and the earth, and in the night and the day.

God brings the living out of the dead, such as a human from a drop of semen and a bird from an egg, and He brings the dead out of the living, such as semen from a human and an egg from a bird. And He brings the earth back to life with vegetation after its dryness and aridity. Likewise, O people, you will be brought out of your graves alive for reckoning and recompense.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 30, verse 20:

Among the signs of God that point to His greatness and the perfection of His power is that He created your father Adam from dust. Then you are human beings who multiply and spread across the earth, seeking of God's bounty.

Among His signs, which demonstrate His greatness and the perfection of His power, is that He created for you, O men, mates from your own kind, so that you may find tranquility in them and dwell with them. He placed between the wife and her husband affection and mercy. Indeed, in God's creation of this are signs demonstrating God's power and His oneness, for a people who reflect and ponder.

Among the signs of God's power: the creation of the heavens and their elevation without pillars, the creation of the earth despite its vastness and extension, and the difference of your languages and the variety of your colours. Indeed, in this are lessons for everyone who has knowledge and insight.

Among the signs of this power is that Allah made sleep a rest for you, whether at night or during the day, for in sleep there is the attainment of rest and the removal of fatigue. And He made the day for you, a time in which you disperse to seek provision. Indeed, in that are signs of the perfection of Allah's power and the effectiveness of His will, for a people who listen to admonitions with reflection, contemplation and consideration.

Among the signs of His power, glorified is He, is that He shows you the lightning, so that you fear the thunderbolts and hope for the rain. He sends down rain from the clouds, by which He revives the earth after its barrenness and dryness. Indeed, in this is a clear proof of the perfection of Allah's power, the greatness of His wisdom, and His kindness to everyone who has a mind with which to be guided.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 30, verse 25:

Among His signs that show His power is the standing of the heavens and the earth, their being fixed and steady by His command, so that they do not shake, and the heaven does not fall upon the earth. Then, when Allah calls you to resurrection on the Day of Judgment, behold, you will come out of the graves swiftly.

To Allah alone belongs everyone in the heavens and the earth: the angels, mankind, the jinn, animals, plants, and inanimate things. All of these are submissive to His command and humbled before His perfection.

Allah alone is the One who originates creation from nothing and then restores it to life after death. Restoring creation to life after death is easier for Allah than originating their creation, though both are equally easy for Him. To Him belongs the highest description in everything that is described, "There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing" (﴿لَيْسَ كَمِثْلِهِ شَيْءٌ ۖ وَهُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْبَصِيرُ﴾). He is the Mighty (al-'Aziz) who cannot be overcome, the Wise (al-Hakim) in His sayings and His deeds, and in His management of the affairs of His creation.

Allah sets forth for you an example from yourselves, O polytheists: Do you have among your slaves and bondmaids any partners in what We have provided you, so that you are equal with them in it, and you fear them as you fear one another among the free partners in your wealth? Thus do you not accept this for yourselves, so how do you accept it for Allah, by making for Him partners from among His creation? In this way We make clear the proofs and arguments for people of sound minds who benefit from them.

Rather, the polytheists followed their desires by imitating their forefathers without knowledge, so they shared with them in ignorance and misguidance. No one can guide those whom Allah has left to stray because of their persistence in disbelief and obstinacy, and these people have no helpers who can rescue them from the punishment of Allah.

So establish your face (toward) the religion, [O Messenger, you and those who follow you], and persevere in the religion that Allah has prescribed for you, which is Islam, the nature upon which Allah created mankind. So your remaining upon it and your adherence to it means adhering to the fitrah (innate disposition) of Allah, of faith in Allah alone. "There is no alteration in the creation of Allah" (﴿لَا تَبْدِيلَ لِخَلْقِ اللَّهِ﴾) and His religion. It is the straight path that leads to the pleasure of Allah, the Lord of the worlds, and to His Paradise. "But most of the people do not know" (﴿وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾), that what I have commanded you with, O Messenger, is the true religion, to the exclusion of all others.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 30, verse 31:

And turn back (in repentance) to Allah and sincerely devote your deeds to Him, and fear Him by carrying out His commands and avoiding His prohibitions, and establish the prayer complete with its pillars, obligatory acts and conditions, and do not be among the polytheists who associate others with Allah in worship.

Do not be among the polytheists, nor among the people of whims and innovations, who altered their religion and changed it, taking some of it and abandoning some of it, following their own desires. They became sects and factions, partisan to their leaders, their parties and their opinions, each helping the other in falsehood. Each party, rejoicing and pleased with what they have, judges for themselves that they are upon the truth and that others are upon falsehood.

When hardship and affliction befall people, they call upon their Lord, turning to Him sincerely, asking Him to remove the harm from them. But when He shows them mercy and removes their harm, behold, a group of them return to associating partners with Him once again, worshipping others alongside Allah.

So that they may deny what We have given them and the favor We have bestowed upon them by removing harm and lifting hardship from them. So enjoy yourselves, O polytheists, in the ease and abundance of this world, for you will soon know what punishment and retribution you will face.
Or have We sent down to these polytheists a clear proof and a decisive book, which speaks in support of their polytheism and their disbelief in God and His signs?

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 30, verse 36:

And when We let the people taste mercy, they rejoice in it; but if an evil befalls them because of what their own hands have sent forth, behold, they despair.

Explanation: When We bestow upon people a blessing of health, well-being and ease, they rejoice in it with the joy of arrogance and exultation, not the joy of gratitude. And if affliction of illness, poverty, fear and constriction befalls them because of their sins and disobediences, they immediately despair of that affliction ever being removed. This is the disposition of most people, in times of ease and in times of hardship.

Do they not know that God expands provision for whomever He wills as a trial: will they give thanks or be ungrateful? And He restricts it for whomever He wills as a test: will they be patient or despairing? Indeed, in that expansion and restriction are signs for a people who believe in God and understand God's wisdom and mercy.

Give, O believer, your relative his right of kinship, through maintaining ties and charity and all other acts of righteousness. Give also to the poor man who does not possess what suffices him and meets his need, and to the needy wayfarer who has been cut off from his way, [giving him] of zakah and charity. That giving is better for those who seek by their deed the Face of Allah, and those who perform these acts and other acts of goodness, they are the successful ones who attain the reward of Allah and are saved from His punishment.

The Noble Qur'an Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 30, verse 39:

Whatever you give as a loan of money, seeking through it an increase (riba) and desiring that the loan grow in addition to the wealth of people, it does not increase in the sight of Allah. But whatever you give in zakah and charity to those deserving it, seeking the pleasure of Allah and desiring His reward, this is what Allah accepts and multiplies for you many times over.

Allah alone is the One who created you, O people, then provided for you in this life, then will cause you to die when your terms come to an end, then will resurrect you from the graves alive for reckoning and recompense. Is there any of your associates who does any of these things? Exalted and sanctified is Allah above the partners these polytheists associate with Him.

Corruption has appeared on land and sea, such as drought, scarcity of rain, and the spread of diseases and epidemics. This is because of the sins that people commit, so that He may make them taste the punishment for some of their deeds that they did in this world, so that they may repent to God, Glorified is He, and turn back from sin, and their affairs will be set right and their conditions will be made upright.

Say, [O Messenger], to those who deny what you have brought: "Travel through the lands with the travel of reflection and contemplation, and look at how the end of the earlier nations who denied was, such as the people of Noah, 'Ad, and Thamud. You will find their end to be the worst of ends and their final state the worst of final states. For most of them were associating partners with Allah."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 30, verse 43:

So direct your face, O Messenger, toward the upright religion, which is Islam, carrying out its commands and avoiding its prohibitions, and hold fast to it before the Day of Resurrection comes. When that Day comes, which no one can turn back, creation will be divided into scattered groups, each differing from the others, so that they may be shown their deeds.

Whoever disbelieves, upon him is the punishment of his disbelief, which is his abiding forever in the Fire. And whoever believes and does righteous deeds, they are preparing for themselves the abodes of Paradise, because of their adherence to obedience to their Lord.

Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar, "the Simplified Tafsir," tafsir meaning explanatory commentary of the Qur'an) on surah 30, verse 45:

So that Allah may reward those who believe in Allah and His Messenger and do righteous deeds, out of His bounty and His favor. Indeed, He does not love the disbelievers, out of His wrath and anger toward them.

Among the signs of God that show He alone is the true God, with no partner, and show the greatness of His power is His sending of the winds ahead of the rain as bearers of good news, stirring up the clouds, so that souls rejoice at this. And that He may let you taste of His mercy, by sending down the rain through which lands and creatures are made to live, and that the ships may run upon the sea by God's command and will, and that you may seek of His bounty through trade and other means. God does this so that you may give thanks for His blessings and worship Him alone.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 30, verse 47:

We certainly sent messengers before you, O Messenger, to their peoples, bringing good news and warning, calling them to monotheism (tawhid) and warning them against associating partners with God (shirk). They came to them with miracles and clear proofs, but most of them disbelieved in their Lord. So We took retribution against those among them who had earned evil deeds, and We destroyed them, and We gave victory to the believers, the followers of the messengers. And likewise We do with those who deny you, if they persist in denying you and do not believe.

Allah, glory be to Him, is the One who sends the winds, and they stir up clouds heavy with water. Allah spreads them across the sky however He wills and makes them into scattered pieces, so you see the rain coming out from between the clouds. Then when He drives it to His servants, behold, they rejoice and are glad, because Allah has turned it toward them.
And indeed they had been, before the rain was sent down, in utter despair and hopelessness, because of its withholding from them.

Look, O observer, with the look of reflection and contemplation, at the effects of the rain on plants, crops and trees: how God gives life to the earth with it after its death, so that He makes it grow and bring forth vegetation. Indeed, the One who is able to revive this earth is surely the One who gives life to the dead, and He is over all things Powerful, nothing can overcome Him.

"And if We were to send a corrupting wind upon their crops and vegetation, and they saw their vegetation had been spoiled by that wind, turning yellow after its greenness, they would indeed, after seeing it, continue to disbelieve in Allah and deny His blessings."

Indeed, you, O Messenger, cannot make hear those whose hearts are dead, or who have stopped up their ears against hearing the truth. So do not grieve or feel sorrow over the disbelief of these polytheists in you, for they are like the deaf and the dead, who do not hear, nor perceive even when they are present. How much more so when they are absent from you and turning their backs?

You, O Messenger, cannot guide those whom Allah has blinded from the path of guidance. You can only make hear, so as to benefit, those who believe in Our verses; they are the ones who submit and comply with the command of Allah.

Allah, the Exalted, is the One who created you from a weak, despised fluid, which is the sperm-drop (nutfah). Then He made, after the weakness of childhood, the strength of youth and its completion. Then He made, after this strength, the weakness of old age and decrepitude. Allah creates what He wills of weakness and strength, and He is the All-Knowing of His creation, the All-Powerful over everything.

On the Day the Hour comes, Allah will raise the creatures from their graves. The polytheists will swear that they remained in the world for only a brief span of time. They lied in their oath, just as they used to lie in the world, and they will be turned away from the truth that the messengers brought.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 30, verse 56:

Those who were given knowledge and faith in God, from among the angels, the prophets and the believers, will say: "You have remained, according to what God wrote and what He had already decreed in His knowledge, from the day you were created until you were resurrected. This is the Day of Resurrection, but you did not know it. You denied it in the world and you called it a lie."

On the Day of Resurrection, the excuses that the wrongdoers offer will not benefit them, and they will not be asked to seek God's pleasure through repentance and obedience. Rather, they will be punished for their evil deeds and disobedience.

We have certainly explained to people in this Qur'an every kind of example, so as to establish the proof against them and to affirm the Oneness of Allah, exalted is He. And if you were to bring them, O Messenger, any sign that indicates your truthfulness, those who disbelieve in you would surely say: "You (O Messenger, and those who follow you) are only people of falsehood in what you bring us of matters."
Like that sealing, Allah seals the hearts of those who do not know the truth of what you bring them, O Messenger, from Allah, of these lessons and clear signs.

So be patient, O Messenger, over the harm your people inflict on you and their denial of you. Indeed, what Allah has promised you of victory, empowerment and reward is true, without any doubt. Do not let those who have no certainty about the promise, and who do not believe in the Resurrection and the recompense, drive you to abandon your religion.
